target_customer: Data teams and analysts at enterprises such as banks (HSBC, ING and Alior are named customer logos) that prepare and blend data
problem: Preparing and blending data takes slow, repeated manual work or code; Enso offers a visual and textual data preparation workflow tool that saves time.
business_model: Open source core with paid cloud and enterprise products

founders.name: Sylwia Brodacka
founders.background_notes: YC bio: leader, software developer, physicist, worked on materials design. A co-founder (Wojciech Danilo) appears only in aggregator search results and is not recorded. Employers and education not listed.

competitors.name: Alteryx
competitors.what: Self-service data preparation and analytics workflow software
competitors.traction_then: Named by TechCrunch at the April 2022 launch as an existing tool alongside Tableau Prep and Knime
competitors.funding_then: Public company; not stated in source

competitors.name: Tableau Prep
competitors.traction_then: Named in the same TechCrunch article

technical_complexity.rationale: A new visual and textual programming language with a runtime and tooling, built over several years, is substantial engineering.

defensibility.rationale: The custom language and workflows create lock in and are costly to rebuild, but open source licensing and large rivals limit exclusivity.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Established data preparation vendors existed at the time; no source shows copying or acquisition of Enso.

market_need_then: Enterprises had a large analyst population needing data preparation, shown by the entrenched use of Alteryx and Tableau Prep named in 2022 press.

branding.name_origin: Enso is the renamed Luna visual language project; the team said a new name captures the aim but did not state the meaning in the page read.

rebrands.why: Luna is a common term and very close to the programming language Lua, causing confusion (per the project's first dev blog).

branding.community_and_virality: Open source project on GitHub with a community around the language

brand_strength.rationale: A rename avoided a confusable name and the project has an open source community, but no press about the brand itself was found.

outcome_analysis: Enso, previously the Luna language project, joined YC in Summer 2021 and emerged from stealth in April 2022 with a $16.5M round led by investors including SignalFire and Khosla. It positions itself as an Alteryx alternative with enterprise banking customers and about 20 to 26 staff. Founding history is long and the market has strong incumbents, but it remained active in 2026.
notes: The round is labeled Series A in the company news URL, while CB Insights calls it seed; recorded as series_a per the company link, which was not opened. Competitor sources are about eight months after the batch since no earlier dated source was found. Founding year is 2018 per YC; other sources say the Luna project began in 2015. Brodacka is listed as a co-founder alongside Wojciech Danilo in aggregator results only. Relationship between Enso Analytics and the enso-org GitHub project is inferred from shared name and README.
